speaker: narrator
text: On Thursday, Anthropic, the maker of the chatbot Claude, raised eighty-one billion dollars in the biggest stock market debut ever.

speaker: narrator
text: , when a company sells pieces of itself, called shares, to investors for the first time.

speaker: narrator
text: Anthropic sold nine hundred and eighty million shares at eighty-three dollars each.

speaker: narrator
text: The old record: the rocket company SpaceX, about seventy-five billion, in June.

speaker: narrator
text: Then the shares hit the Nasdaq.

speaker: narrator
text: The first trade: a hundred and eleven fifty, over thirty percent above eighty-three.

speaker: narrator
text: By the end of the day: ninety-seven seventeen.

speaker: narrator
text: Still above eighty-three, but anyone who paid that first price was down thirteen percent.

speaker: narrator
text: The day before, the crypto app Binance Wallet sold up to five hundred million dollars of tokens built to follow Anthropic's price.

speaker: narrator
text: But a token isn't a share.

speaker: narrator
text: No vote, no cut of any profits paid out, just the price moves.

speaker: narrator
text: Check the price you'd actually pay: day one moved thirteen percent.

speaker: narrator
text: And a token that tracks a stock isn't the stock.

speaker: narrator
text: The vote and the payouts stay with the shares.
